title: Calming strategies
examples: What can I do when I feel really cross?
Can you show me how to take a big breath?
Where is the quiet corner in the classroom?

explain.say: Sometimes you have big feelings. You can learn ways to help your body feel calm.
Try belly breathing. Put a hand on your tummy. Breathe in slowly through your nose.

draw.text: Belly breathing: breathe in, breathe out.

explain.say: Your tummy moves out when you breathe in. Then breathe out slowly. Your tummy moves in.

draw.text: Breathe in: tummy out. Breathe out: tummy in.

explain.say: You can also count slowly to ten. Breathe out slowly as you count.
You can go to a quiet space for a short rest. Tell a grown-up where you are going.

draw.text: A quiet space for a short rest

explain.say: A jigsaw is hard, and you feel cross. Take three slow breaths. Then try again, or ask for help.

faq.q: What should I do if I feel angry?
faq.a: You can try taking three slow, deep belly breaths. This helps your body feel safer.
asks: How do I calm down fast?

faq.q: Is counting always a good way to calm down?
faq.a: Counting helps many people. You can also try slow breaths or a quiet space. Use the one that helps you.
asks: Is counting okay when I am upset?

faq.a: A quiet space is a calm spot where you can sit for a few minutes. A grown-up knows where you are.
asks: Where can I go to be quiet?

faq.q: Do I have to breathe with my tummy?
faq.a: You can choose. Belly breathing is one way to take a slow, deep breath. Any slow breath can help.

faq.q: Can I use all these things at once?
faq.a: It is best to choose just one thing to try first. Pick one strategy that sounds easy right now.
asks: Which one should I start with?

facts: Deep breathing helps send calm messages to your brain.
Counting helps to focus your mind when you feel overwhelmed.
A quiet space gives your body time to rest and recharge.
It is okay to need help when your feelings are big.

quiz.say: Amira feels upset. Tap a good first thing to try.
quiz.why: Slow belly breaths help your body calm down. You can do them anywhere.

wrong.0: Shouting can make the big feeling feel even bigger.
wrong.2: Throwing toys can hurt someone or break the toys.

quiz.say: You need a short rest. Tap a good place to go.
quiz.why: A quiet corner is calm and safe. A grown-up can see you there.

wrong.0: Lots of noise can make big feelings feel bigger.
wrong.1: Going outside alone is unsafe, so stay where a grown-up can see you.

quiz.say: Put a hand on your tummy. Breathe in. Tap what it does.
quiz.show: ✋ Hand on tummy. Breathe in slowly.
quiz.why: When you breathe in deeply, your tummy moves out. When you breathe out, it moves in.

wrong.1: Your tummy moves in when you breathe out.
wrong.2: Keep your hand on your tummy and feel it move as you breathe in.
